user: At 16:30 on 6 January Bus_29 is within its limits but close to them. Why is it so close, compared with a moment when it had a comfortable margin?

grid.name: PGLib IEEE 30-Bus System (Alsac–Stott)
grid.description: Synthetic 7-day profile generated from the bundled PGLib IEEE 30-bus (Alsac–Stott) MATPOWER case: five dispatchable units with their own costs, line ratings from PGLib.

result.method: Every combination of the factors, each at its value now or in the reference state, was solved by AC power flow. A factor's share is its Shapley value — its average effect over every order in which the changes could have happened — so the shares add up to the change, interactions included.

assistant:
At **16:30**, Bus_29 was at **0.965 p.u.**—inside the **0.950 p.u.** lower limit, with **0.015 p.u.** of margin. At the comfortable-margin comparison point, **05:15**, it was **0.982 p.u.**, leaving **0.032 p.u.** The voltage had fallen by **0.016 p.u.**

The main reason was increased demand nearby: demand at Bus_28 and Bus_29 rose from **8.76 MW to 11.15 MW**, accounting for about **74%** of the voltage drop. Bus_29’s own demand increased by **1.95 MW**. Higher demand elsewhere contributed the remaining **26%**. The change in generator output was negligible and was ruled out as a cause. The finding that nearby demand was the main cause held against other reference moments checked.

📋 Data source: measurements
